- When sentiment is negative and forecast is trending down, model tends to underestimate future prices — correct by adding 1–2% to forecast for mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots in subsequent days — reduce forecast by 1–3% for 2–5 day lag.
- If sentiment is positive and forecast is flat or slightly declining, model underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast by 1–3% for 3–7 day horizon.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model exhibits persistent downward bias — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with recent price action.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates final 5–10 days — apply a 1–2% upward correction for the last 5–10 days of forecast horizon.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, model fails to catch momentum — increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per day for 3–7 days ahead.
